page: UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-384GB-2xL4 is a GPU-accelerated server configured on the KVM hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing 12.0 GB per core. Acceleration is delivered via two NVIDIA L4 GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a combined 48 GB of VRAM. This instance does not include local storage.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in several areas. The AMD EPYC CPU achieves top-tier single-core and multi-core scores in Geekbench, alongside top-tier single-core stress-ng performance. Large-block memory bandwidth is strong, though the Passmark memory score sits in the average tier. For AI workloads, the dual NVIDIA L4 GPUs deliver top-tier LLM inference speeds, processing 2805.36 tokens per second for prompt processing and 54.14 tokens per second for text generation on a medium 7B model.

The absence of bundled local storage requires users to provision external block storage, which may impact sequential I/O performance depending on the network configuration. The shared CPU allocation is another architectural tradeoff to consider for sustained maximum compute workloads. Given the hardware profile, this server is suited for machine learning inference, data science pipelines, and GPU-accelerated rendering or simulation tasks that require substantial system memory alongside dedicated graphics accelerators.
